comments.value: Flags are not used for languages on the website or in VRChat.

details:
Hi,
TL;DR: The US flag is used to indicate the EN language. Please change it to the EN (not GB) flag. 
Explanation:
English is used by approximately 2 billion people, the majority of which live in neither the UK nor the US. Because of this and to remove ambiguity, the St George's Cross (aka the flag of the 'state' of England, not the country of the UK) is the internationally recognised flag denoting the English language. 
The International Standards Organisation - which the US is party to - indicates in ISO 639-4:2010 that the least ambigious solution of using the St Georges Cross to denote the language of english *UNLESS* a culture parameter is inferred (EN vs en_us/en_gb). As no option exists for one to select their culture, EN should indicate English and be denoted using the flag of England.
Currently, in VR chat, the US flag is used to denote English language. This creates ambiguity as a culture symbol is being used to indicate a language, thereby implying that there IS a en_gb indicator available too (the GB flag), when there is not.
It is the equivalent of putting the flag of Mexico or Argentina for the "Spanish" language selection. It might make sense to a minority of users, but the rest are just confused.
I am willing to accept the Judgement of Solomon solution of cutting the metaphorical baby in half, and have you use the Australian flag instead. 
Thank you for your time,
EN: Goodbye!
en_gb: Cheers!
en_us: Seeya!
en_au: G'day mate!
title: Incorrect/Ambigious Language Flag Convention
